subject: chemistry
title: Nanoparticles
key_idea: Nanoparticles are 1 to 100 nm across, only a few hundred atoms. They have a very high surface area to volume ratio, so they behave differently from the same material in bulk and smaller amounts are needed. They have many uses, but their long-term risks are not yet known.

blocks.text: This topic is for separate science chemistry only. Nanoparticles sit between molecules and everyday dust. This section covers their size and how to convert it.

items.meaning: One billionth of a metre, 1 × 10⁻⁹ m.
A particle 1 to 100 nm across, of the order of a few hundred atoms.
The study of structures that are 1 to 100 nm in size.

blocks.label: Converting nanometres to metres
where: size in m: the length in metres
size in nm: the length in nanometres
blocks.formula: size in m = size in nm × 10⁻⁹

blocks.text: So 90 nm is 9.0 × 10⁻⁸ m. In order of size, smallest first: proton, atom, molecule, nanoparticle.

items: A nanoparticle is 1 to 100 nm across.
Nanoparticles are smaller than fine particles and much smaller than coarse particles (dust).

blocks.text: Nanoparticles have a very high surface area compared with their volume. This section covers how to calculate the ratio for a cube.

blocks.label: Surface area of a cube
where: side: length of one edge, in nm

blocks.label: Volume of a cube
where: side: length of one edge, in nm

items.text: For a cube with sides 10 nm: 6 × 10² = 600 nm².

diagram.alt: Change the side length of a cube-shaped nanoparticle and watch the surface area, volume and surface area to volume ratio change.

items: As the side of a cube decreases by a factor of 10, the surface area to volume ratio increases by a factor of 10.
Nanoparticles may have different properties from the same material in bulk, because of their high surface area to volume ratio.
Smaller quantities are needed to be effective than for normal-sized particles.
Smaller particles have a higher surface area to volume ratio.
Surface area = 6 × side², volume = side³, then divide.

blocks.text: Nanoparticles are used in many products. This section covers some uses and the possible risks.

rows: Block UV light, and are transparent so they leave no white marks
High surface area to volume ratio, so reactions are faster and less catalyst is needed
A much thinner layer can be used, so more light passes through
Silver kills bacteria, which stops smells and infections
Can carry medication inside the body

items: The long-term risks are not yet known, because nanoparticles are new technology.
They could be breathed in, absorbed through the skin or enter the bloodstream.
They could have toxic effects or catalyse harmful reactions in the body.
Some take a long time to break down in the environment.
Uses come from the high surface area to volume ratio or the tiny size.
The risks are mostly unknown long-term effects if they enter the body.
Evaluate a use by weighing the benefits against the risks.

checks.q: A cube-shaped nanoparticle has sides of 10 nm. Calculate its surface area to volume ratio.
checks.a: Surface area = 6 × 10² = 600 nm². Volume = 10³ = 1000 nm³. Ratio = 600 ÷ 1000 = 0.6.

checks.q: Explain why nanoparticles are good catalysts.
checks.a: They have a large surface area to volume ratio, so reactions take place on more of the surface and the reaction is faster.

checks.q: Give one possible risk of using nanoparticles in sun cream.
checks.a: They could be absorbed through the skin into the bloodstream, or the long-term risks are not known.

worked_example.question: Zinc oxide can be produced as nanoparticles and as fine particles. A nanoparticle of zinc oxide is a cube of side 82 nm. Calculate the surface area of a nanoparticle of zinc oxide. Give your answer in standard form.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each step. A cube has six equal faces.

worked_example.question: Some sunscreens contain nanoparticles of titanium dioxide. Explain why nanoparticles of titanium dioxide are used in some sunscreens.
answer_points: They reflect, absorb or block UV light, so they prevent sunburn or skin damage.
The nanoparticles are very small, less than 100 nm, so they give better skin coverage and cannot be seen on the skin, because they are clear or colourless.
worked_example.tip: Any two points score one mark each. Link each property to its purpose.

worked_example.question: A cube-shaped nanoparticle has sides of length 10 nm. Calculate the surface area to volume ratio of the cube. Use the equation: surface area to volume ratio = surface area ÷ volume.
worked_example.tip: A correct final answer scores all three marks. Do not write the ratio the wrong way round.
